blocks.prompt: 3 (i) [printed as 2 (i)] Sketch the region bounded by the given curves and find the area of the region: \(y = 2x,\ y = x^{2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh "do curves ke darmiyan area" wala sawal hai. Is ke liye do cheezein chahiye: curves kahan milti hain (yehi limits hain), aur kaunsi curve upar hai.
Formula: \(A = \int_a^b [f(x) - g(x)]\,dx\), jahan \(f\) upar wali aur \(g\) neeche wali curve hai (3.7.1 ka Note 5).
Pehle sketch banana is liye zaroori hai ke tasveer se foran nazar aa jata hai ke upar kaun hai.
Plan: intersection points, upar wali curve, phir integral.
steps:
Diya gaya: line \(y = 2x\) aur parabola \(y = x^{2}\).
Maloom karna: region ka sketch aur us ka area.
Tareeqa: Do curves ke darmiyan area = integral of (upar wali minus neeche wali). Yeh formula is liye kaam karta hai ke har patli strip ki height upar aur neeche wali curve ka farq hoti hai.

Qadam 1: Intersection points
\[x^{2} = 2x \Rightarrow x(x - 2) = 0\]
\[x = 0 \text{ ya } x = 2\]
Points: \((0, 0)\) aur \((2, 4)\).
Kyun: Region wahin band hota hai jahan dono curves milti hain. Dono \(y\) barabar rakh kar equation banayi.
Dhyan dein: Dono taraf \(x\) se divide mat kijiye, warna \(x = 0\) wala root kho jayega; factor bana kar hal kijiye.

Qadam 2: Upar kaun hai?
\(x = 1\) par: line \(2(1) = 2\), parabola \(1^{2} = 1\). Is liye \([0, 2]\) par \(y = 2x\) upar hai.
Kyun: Integrand hamesha (upar) minus (neeche) hona chahiye taake area positive aaye. Sketch mein bhi line parabola ke upar nazar aati hai.

Qadam 3: Integrate karein
\[A = \int_0^2 (2x - x^{2})\,dx\]
\[= \left[x^{2} - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_0^2 = 4 - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: Har term par power rule: \(\int 2x\,dx = x^{2}\), \(\int x^{2}dx = \frac{x^{3}}{3}\). Lower limit 0 par sab terms zero hain, is liye sirf upper limit ki value bachi.

Tasdeeq:
Ek mufeed shortcut: parabola \(y = x^{2}\) aur kisi line ke darmiyan area, jab woh \(x = \alpha\) aur \(x = \beta\) par milein, \(\frac{(\beta - \alpha)^{3}}{6}\) hota hai. Yahan \(\frac{2^{3}}{6} = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3}\). Jawab mil gaya.

answer_figure.alt: The line y = 2x and the parabola y = x squared meeting at the origin and at (2, 4); the region between them, with the line on top, is shaded.
answer_figure.caption: Figure: region for Question 3 (i) (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) [printed as 2 (ii)] Sketch the region bounded by the given curves and find the area of the region: \(y = \sqrt{x},\ y = x^{2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi do curves ke darmiyan area hai.
Dono curves origin aur \((1, 1)\) se guzarti hain; in ke darmiyan \(\sqrt{x}\) upar aur \(x^{2}\) neeche hota hai.
Yaad rakhiye: \(\sqrt{x}\) sirf \(x \ge 0\) ke liye defined hai, is liye region bhi right side par hi hai.
Plan: milne ke points, upar wali curve, phir integral.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = \sqrt{x}\) aur \(y = x^{2}\).
Maloom karna: sketch aur band area.
Tareeqa: \(A = \int_a^b (\text{upar} - \text{neeche})\,dx\).

Qadam 1: Intersection points
\[\sqrt{x} = x^{2} \Rightarrow x = x^{4}\]
\[x(x^{3} - 1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0,\ 1\]
Points: \((0, 0)\) aur \((1, 1)\).
Kyun: Dono taraf square kiya taake root khatam ho jaye. Yahan square karna mehfooz hai kyunke \(x \ge 0\) par dono sides non-negative hain, koi faltu (extra) root paida nahi hota.

Qadam 2: Upar kaun hai?
\(x = 0.25\) par: \(\sqrt{0.25} = 0.5\) aur \(0.25^{2} = 0.0625\). Is liye \(y = \sqrt{x}\) upar hai.
Kyun: 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan kisi number ka square root us se bara aur square us se chhota hota hai; misal ke taur par \(\sqrt{0.25} = 0.5\) jabke \(0.25^{2} = 0.0625\).

Qadam 3: Integrate karein
\[A = \int_0^1 \left(x^{1/2} - x^{2}\right)dx\]
\[= \left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2} - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_0^1 = \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x}\) ko \(x^{1/2}\) likha taake power rule lag sake: power ek barhao aur nayi power se divide karo, \(\frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2} = \frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{3/2}\) ka matlab \(\frac{2}{3}\) hai, \(\frac{3}{2}\) nahi.

Tasdeeq:
\(y = \sqrt{x}\) aur \(y = x^{2}\) (\(x \ge 0\)) ek doosre ka line \(y = x\) mein aaina (reflection) hain, is liye \(y = x\) region ko do barabar hisson mein baant deti hai. Ek hissa \(\int_0^1 (x - x^{2})\,dx = \frac{1}{6}\), double \(\frac{1}{3}\). Jawab mil gaya.

answer_figure.alt: The curves y = square root of x and y = x squared meeting at the origin and at (1, 1); the region between them, with the square-root curve on top, is shaded.
answer_figure.caption: Figure: region for Question 3 (ii) (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) [printed as 2 (iii)] Sketch the region bounded by the given curves and find the area of the region: \(y = x^{4} - x^{2},\ y = 1 - x^{2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Do curves ke darmiyan area, aur dono even functions hain (\(x\) ki jagah \(-x\) rakhne se kuch nahi badalta).
Is ka matlab tasveer \(y\)-axis ke dono taraf bilkul ek jaisi hai, aur hum symmetry se kaam aadha kar sakte hain.
Plan: milne ke points, upar wali curve, integral (symmetry ke saath).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = x^{4} - x^{2}\) aur \(y = 1 - x^{2}\).
Maloom karna: sketch aur band area.
Tareeqa: upar minus neeche, aur symmetry ka faida.

Qadam 1: Intersection points
\[x^{4} - x^{2} = 1 - x^{2} \Rightarrow x^{4} = 1\]
\[x = \pm 1\]
Points: \((-1, 0)\) aur \((1, 0)\).
Kyun: Dono taraf \(-x^{2}\) hai jo cancel ho jata hai, aur bohat aasaan equation bachti hai. Real roots sirf \(\pm 1\) hain.

Qadam 2: Upar kaun hai?
\(x = 0\) par: \(1 - 0 = 1\) aur \(0 - 0 = 0\). Is liye \([-1, 1]\) par \(y = 1 - x^{2}\) upar hai.
Kyun: Farq \((1 - x^{2}) - (x^{4} - x^{2}) = 1 - x^{4}\) hai jo \(|x| \le 1\) par kabhi negative nahi hota. Yani integrand bhi seedha \(1 - x^{4}\) ban gaya.

Qadam 3: Integrate karein
\[A = \int_{-1}^{1}(1 - x^{4})\,dx = 2\int_0^1 (1 - x^{4})\,dx\]
\[= 2\left[x - \dfrac{x^{5}}{5}\right]_0^1 = 2\cdot\dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{8}{5}\]
Kyun: \(1 - x^{4}\) even function hai, is liye \(-1\) se \(1\) tak ka integral \(0\) se \(1\) tak ke integral ka double hai. Is se negative numbers ke saath hisaab ki zaroorat khatam ho gayi.
Dhyan dein: Neeche wali curve \(x^{4} - x^{2}\) ka kuch hissa axis ke neeche hai, lekin hum farq integrate kar rahe hain, is liye alag torna nahi parta.

Tasdeeq:
Symmetry ke baghair: \(\left[x - \frac{x^{5}}{5}\right]_{-1}^{1} = \frac{4}{5} - \left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) = \frac{8}{5}\). Wohi jawab.

answer_figure.alt: The curves y = 1 minus x squared (an arch with top (0, 1)) and y = x to the fourth minus x squared (a W shape) meeting at (minus 1, 0) and (1, 0); the region between them is shaded.
answer_figure.caption: Figure: region for Question 3 (iii) (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 3 (iv) [printed as 2 (iv)] Sketch the region bounded by the given curves and find the area of the region: \(y = x^{2}\) and \(y = |x|\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan \(y = |x|\) aur \(y = x^{2}\) ke darmiyan area chahiye.
Absolute value (modulus) ka matlab hai ke yeh "V" shakal ki do lines hain: \(x \ge 0\) par \(y = x\) aur \(x < 0\) par \(y = -x\).
Is liye do barabar chhote regions bante hain, ek dayen aur ek bayen.
Plan: milne ke points, symmetry, \([0, 1]\) par integral aur phir double.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = x^{2}\) aur \(y = |x|\).
Maloom karna: sketch aur band area.
Tareeqa: \(|x|\) ko sign ke hisaab se toro; dono graphs \(y\)-axis ke gird symmetric hain.

Qadam 1: Intersection points
\(x \ge 0\) ke liye: \(x^{2} = x \Rightarrow x = 0, 1\).
\(x < 0\) ke liye: \(x^{2} = -x \Rightarrow x = -1\).
Points: \((-1, 1)\), \((0, 0)\), \((1, 1)\).
Kyun: \(|x|\) ke saath seedha equation hal nahi hoti; pehle us ki jagah \(x\) ya \(-x\) rakhna parta hai.
Dhyan dein: Sirf \(x^{2} = x\) hal kar ke \(x = -1\) wala point bhool jana aam ghalti hai.

Qadam 2: Upar kaun hai?
\(x = 0.5\) par: \(|x| = 0.5\), \(x^{2} = 0.25\). Is liye \([-1, 1]\) par \(y = |x|\) upar hai.
Kyun: Jab \(|x| < 1\) ho to square karne se number chhota ho jata hai, is liye parabola V ke neeche rehta hai.

Qadam 3: Symmetry se integrate karein
\[A = 2\int_0^1 (x - x^{2})\,dx\]
\[= 2\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_0^1 = 2\cdot\dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: Bayen taraf ka region dayen wale ka aaina hai, aur \([0, 1]\) par \(|x| = x\) hai. Ek region ka area nikal kar double kar diya.

Tasdeeq:
Bayan region seedha: \(\int_{-1}^{0}(-x - x^{2})\,dx = \left[-\frac{x^{2}}{2} - \frac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{0} = 0 - \left(-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{6}\). Dayen wale ke barabar, jaisa hona chahiye tha.

answer_figure.alt: The V-shaped graph y = |x| and the parabola y = x squared meeting at (minus 1, 1), the origin and (1, 1); the two small regions between them are shaded.
answer_figure.caption: Figure: region for Question 3 (iv) (original drawing)
